attributes.cardDescription: Enum field classifying which round of the interview loop a Meeting represents (phone screen, technical, onsite, panel, final)
attributes.readMe:
# Interview Round Field

## Summary
A StringField enum (phone-screen | technical | onsite | panel | final) built with `enumField`, naming which stage of a multi-round interview loop a given `Meeting` represents.

## Import
```ts
import { InterviewRoundField, INTERVIEW_ROUND_OPTIONS } from './interview-round-field';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

It is a **primitive** FieldDef (extends `StringField`), so it serializes as a
bare string and cannot hold `containedExamples` — the linked example is a
card that actually carries the field.

**1. `Meeting.roundType`** — shown in the Meeting isolated view's Details
panel next to `meetingType`, distinguishing "this interview is the technical
round" from "this interview is the final round" for the same candidate.

**2. `ScheduleInterviewInput.roundType`** (in
`commands/schedule-interview-command.gts`) — the input a caller sets when
scripting a new interview meeting, so the created Meeting is classified from
the moment it exists.

**3. Distinguishing a candidate's multiple Meetings.** A candidate can have
several linked interview Meetings (e.g. `interview-amara-1` and
`interview-amara-2`); `roundType` is what tells them apart on the Candidate's
interview-feedback list beyond just the date.

## Template Usage
```hbs
<@fields.roundType @format='atom' @displayContainer={{false}} />
```

**Non-goals:** meeting *type* (interview vs one-on-one vs standup — see
`Meeting.meetingType` / `MeetingTypeField` for that); scheduling logic or
conflict detection.

**Example in use:** `Meeting/interview-amara-1` carries `roundType:
technical`.
